rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Ramadan above the other months because He chose it for the descent of the great Qur’an; revelation of earlier divine books also occurred in this month.
rows.anchor: يمدح تعالى شهر الصيام من بين سائر الشهور، بأن اختاره من بينهن لإنزال القرآن العظيم فيه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ahmad says Abraham’s scrolls came down on Ramadan’s first night, the Torah on its sixth, the Gospel on its thirteenth, and the Qur’an on its twenty-fourth.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أنزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from Jabir that the Zabur descended on Ramadan’s twelfth night and the Gospel on its eighteenth, with the remaining dates as in the preceding report.
rows.anchor: وقد روي من حديث جابر بن عبد الله وفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scriptures each descended all at once to their respective prophets, whereas the Qur’an first descended whole to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then piecemeal to Muhammad according to events.
rows.anchor: وأما القرآن فإنما نزل جملة واحدة إلى بيت العزة من السماء الدنيا، وكان ذلك في شهر رمضان، في ليلة القدر منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Replying to ʿAtiyya al-Aswad’s concern that revelation occurred in other months, Ibn ʿAbbas said the Qur’an descended whole in Ramadan on the blessed Night of Decree, then gradually across months and days.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: إنه أنزل في رمضان، في ليلة القدر وفي ليلة مباركة جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s report, Ibn ʿAbbas says the Qur’an descended to the lowest heaven and Bayt al-ʿIzza midway through Ramadan, then came to the Prophet over twenty years in response to people’s words.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: أنزل القرآن في النصف من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿIkrima’s report, Ibn ʿAbbas says the Qur’an descended whole to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr; God then supplied the Prophet’s responses whenever the polytheists raised an argument.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: نزل القرآن في شهر رمضان في ليلة القدر إلى هذه السماء الدنيا جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports connect the gradual replies to the Qur’an’s statement that disbelievers asked why it was not revealed all at once and that God answered their challenges with truth and the best explanation.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

rows.speaker: فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din allows another possibility: on each Night of Decree, the amount people needed was sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه كان ينزل في كل ليلة قدر ما يحتاج الناس إلى إنزاله إلى مثله من اللوح إلى سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din leaves undecided whether this annual partial descent or the earlier account of a single descent is more likely.
rows.anchor: وتوقف، هل هذا أولى أو الأول؟

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi attributes the annual-descent possibility to Muqatil ibn Hayyan and reports consensus that the Qur’an descended whole from the Preserved Tablet to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: وحكى الإجماع على أن القرآن نزل جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى بيت العزة في السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and others are reported to interpret the verse as referring to the Qur’an’s virtue or to the obligation of fasting in Ramadan; Ibn Kathir calls this very strange.
rows.anchor: أي: في فضله أو وجوب صومه، وهذا غريب جدا

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an guides the hearts of those who believe, affirm, and follow it; its clear proofs are understood by reflection, validate its guidance, oppose error, and distinguish truth from falsehood and lawful from unlawful.
rows.anchor: هدى لقلوب العباد ممن آمن به وصدقه واتبعه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says not to say simply “Ramadan,” because Ramadan is one of God’s names, but to say “the month of Ramadan”; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits it through Abu Maʿshar from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and Saʿid al-Maqburi.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لا تقولوا: رمضان، فإن رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim says similar disapproval of saying “Ramadan” alone was also reported from Mujahid and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن مجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Thabit allowed saying “Ramadan” without the word “month.”
rows.anchor: ورخص فيه ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Abu Maʿshar Nujayh was an authority in campaigns and biographies but weak as a transmitter.
rows.anchor: أبو معشر هو نجيح بن عبد الرحمن المدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Maʿshar’s son made the report Prophetic, but Ibn ʿAdi rejected that attribution; Ibn Kathir agrees, calling the son abandoned and his elevation of the report an error.
rows.anchor: وقد أنكره عليه الحافظ ابن عدي

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari supports using “Ramadan” alone by titling a chapter “It is said Ramadan” and citing reports such as the promise that fasting Ramadan with faith and seeking reward brings forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقد انتصر البخاري، رحمه الله، في كتابه لهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing Ramadan means being healthy and resident in one’s locality when the month begins; such a person is required to fast.
rows.anchor: إيجاب حتم على من شهد استهلال الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse abrogated the earlier permission for a healthy resident to skip the fast and feed one poor person for each missed day.
rows.anchor: ونسخت هذه الآية الإباحة المتقدمة لمن كان صحيحا مقيما أن يفطر ويفدي بإطعام مسكين عن كل يوم

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ فَعِدَّةٌۭ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person whose illness makes fasting burdensome or harmful, or who is traveling, may break the fast and must make up the same number of days later.
rows.anchor: ومن كان به مرض في بدنه يشق عليه الصيام معه، أو يؤذيه

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concessions for illness and travel, while fasting remains binding on the healthy resident, express divine ease and mercy.
rows.anchor: إنما رخص لكم في الفطر في حال المرض وفي السفر، مع تحتمه في حق المقيم الصحيح، تيسيرا عليكم ورحمة بكم

rows.speaker: طائفة من السلف
rows.claim: A group of early authorities held that someone resident when Ramadan began could not break the fast after traveling mid-month; travel only excused one who entered Ramadan already traveling.
rows.anchor: ذهب طائفة من السلف إلى أن من كان مقيما في أول الشهر ثم سافر في أثنائه

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Hazm attributes the resident-then-travels position to a group of Companions and Successors, though Ibn Kathir questions the accuracy of that attribution.
rows.anchor: نقله أبو محمد بن حزم في كتابه المحلى، عن جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet set out during Ramadan for the conquest of Mecca, traveled as far as al-Kadid, then broke his fast and ordered the people to break theirs; both canonical compilers report it.
rows.anchor: خرج في شهر رمضان لغزوة الفتح

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: طائفة من الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: Some Companions and Successors considered breaking the fast obligatory for a traveler, taking “a number of other days” as a command to break and make up.
rows.anchor: ذهب آخرون من الصحابة والتابعين إلى وجوب الإفطار في السفر

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the majority view that travelers may choose to fast or break; reports say the Prophet’s companions did both without blaming one another.
rows.anchor: والصحيح قول الجمهور، أن الأمر في ذلك على التخيير، وليس بحتم

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that on a very hot Ramadan journey with the Prophet, no one fasted except the Prophet and ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء [قال] (6) خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and a group hold that fasting while traveling is preferable, based on the Prophet’s own practice.
rows.anchor: قالت طائفة منهم الشافعي: الصيام في السفر أفضل من الإفطار، لفعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group prefers breaking the fast to accept the concession, citing the Prophet’s answer that either breaking or fasting is good.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: بل الإفطار أفضل، أخذا بالرخصة

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked about fasting during travel, the Prophet said that the one who breaks the fast does well and there is no blame on the one who fasts.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه سئل عن الصوم في السفر

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A separate Prophetic report urges travelers to take the concession God has granted them.
rows.anchor: عليكم برخصة الله التي رخص لكم

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A third group treats fasting and breaking the fast during travel as equally permissible.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: هما سواء لحديث عائشة

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Hamza ibn ʿAmr al-Aslami asked whether to fast while traveling because he fasted often, the Prophet let him choose either course; the two canonical compilers report it.
rows.anchor: إن شئت فصم، وإن شئت فأفطر

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Some hold that breaking the fast is better when fasting is difficult, relying on the Prophet’s rebuke of fasting under hardship on a journey.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن شق الصيام فالإفطار أفضل لحديث جابر

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Seeing a man shaded while fasting on a journey, the Prophet said that fasting while traveling was not righteousness; al-Bukhari and Muslim report it.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا قد ظلل عليه، فقال

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a traveler is averse to God’s concession and regards breaking the fast as detestable, Ibn Kathir says he must break the fast and fasting is forbidden for him in that state.
rows.anchor: فهذا يتعين عليه الإفطار، ويحرم عليه الصيام، والحالة هذه

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن عمر وجابر وغيرهما
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿUmar, Jabir, and others say that one who refuses God’s concession bears sin like the mountains of ʿArafat.
rows.anchor: من لم يقبل رخصة الله كان عليه من الإثم مثل جبال عرفة

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: One legal view requires make-up fasts to be consecutive because the make-up should mirror the original performance.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه يجب التتابع، لأن القضاء يحكي الأداء

rows.speaker: جمهور السلف والخلف
rows.claim: The majority of early and later scholars allow make-up fasts to be consecutive or separated; the sequence in Ramadan was required by the month’s fixed performance window, while afterward only the number of missed days is due.
rows.anchor: لا يجب التتابع، بل إن شاء فرق، وإن شاء تابع. وهذا قول جمهور السلف والخلف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Bedouin who heard the Prophet reported that the best religion is the easiest religion, repeated twice.
rows.anchor: عن الأعرابي الذي سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: عروة بن الفقيمي
rows.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Fuqaymi reports that after the Prophet prayed with his head dripping from ablution or a bath, he answered questions about possible blame by repeating three times that God’s religion is ease.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبي عروة، قال: كنا ننتظر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s instruction to make matters easy rather than difficult, and to reassure people rather than drive them away; both canonical collections include it.
rows.anchor: يسروا، ولا تعسروا، وسكنوا ولا تنفروا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When sending Muʿadh and Abu Musa to Yemen, the Prophet told them to give good news, ease matters, cooperate, and avoid disagreement; both canonical collections report it.
rows.anchor: بشرا ولا تنفرا، ويسرا ولا تعسرا، وتطاوعا ولا تختلفا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports in the Sunan and Musnads say that the Prophet was sent with the upright, lenient religion.
rows.anchor: بعثت بالحنيفية السمحة

rows.speaker: محجن بن الأدرع
rows.claim: Mahjan ibn al-Adraʿ reports that the Prophet cautioned him not to praise a man’s abundant prayer where the man could hear, lest he ruin him, and said God intended ease for this community.
rows.anchor: عن محجن بن الأدرع: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا يصلي

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted permission to break the fast for illness, travel, and similar excuses to provide ease, then required make-up fasting so the month’s full count would be completed.
rows.anchor: والسفر ونحوهما من الأعذار لإرادته بكم اليسر، وإنما أمركم بالقضاء لتكملوا عدة شهركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to magnify God means remembering Him when worship is completed.
rows.anchor: ولتذكروا الله عند انقضاء عبادتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links remembrance after worship to commands to remember God after pilgrimage, prayer, Friday prayer, before sunset, and at night.
rows.anchor: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic practice establishes the recommendation to glorify, praise, and magnify God after the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: جاءت السنة باستحباب التسبيح، والتحميد والتكبير بعد الصلوات المكتوبات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they recognized that the Prophet had finished his prayer only by hearing him say the takbir.
rows.anchor: ما كنا نعرف انقضاء صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا بالتكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says many scholars infer from this verse that takbir is prescribed at Eid al-Fitr.
rows.anchor: أخذ كثير من العلماء مشروعية التكبير في عيد الفطر من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: داود بن علي الأصبهاني الظاهري
rows.claim: Dawud al-Zahiri holds that Eid al-Fitr takbir is obligatory, based on the apparent command in the verse.
rows.anchor: إلى وجوبه في عيد الفطر؛ لظاهر الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that takbir is not prescribed at Eid al-Fitr.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يشرع التكبير في عيد الفطر

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining scholars recommend Eid al-Fitr takbir, though they differ over details of subsidiary rulings.
rows.anchor: والباقون على استحبابه، على اختلاف في تفاصيل بعض الفروع بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By obeying God’s commands, performing obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and guarding His limits, people may become thankful.
rows.anchor: إذا قمتم بما أمركم الله من طاعته بأداء فرائضه، وترك محارمه، وحفظ حدوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands abundant remembrance after the rites of pilgrimage are completed.
rows.anchor: يأمر تعالى بذكره والإكثار منه بعد قضاء المناسك وفراغها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta, in Ibn Jurayj’s report, explains the comparison as a child constantly saying “my father, my mother”; believers should similarly keep God’s remembrance on their tongues after pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج، عن عطاء

rows.speaker: الضحاك والربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi ibn Anas give the same explanation of constant remembrance, as does Ibn ʿAbbas in al-ʿAwfi’s report.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال الضحاك والربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says pre-Islamic Arabs at pilgrimage boasted that their fathers fed people, bore burdens, and paid blood money, remembering nothing beyond their ancestors’ deeds; God redirected them to remember Him.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك، وأبو وائل، وعطاء بن أبي رباح، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وعطاء الخراساني، والربيع بن أنس، والحسن، وقتادة، ومحمد بن كعب، ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari report that numerous early authorities also explained the verse as displacing boastful remembrance of ancestors with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك، وأبي وائل، وعطاء بن أبي رباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point of the comparison is to urge frequent remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه الحث على كثرة الذكر لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or even greater remembrance” is accusative as a specification (tamyiz), with the implied sense “greater than your remembrance of your fathers.”
rows.anchor: على التمييز، تقديره كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد منه ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “or” confirms that the description is at least equal and possibly greater, rather than expressing doubt, as in the cited comparisons.
rows.anchor: فليست هاهنا للشك قطعا، وإنما هي لتحقيق الخبر عنه بأنه كذلك أو أزيد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After abundant remembrance, God directs people to supplicate, since that is a setting for answered prayer, and censures those who ask only for worldly life while neglecting the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى أرشد إلى دعائه بعد كثرة ذكره، فإنه مظنة الإجابة، وذم من لا يسأله إلا في أمر دنياه

words: وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No share in the Hereafter” means no portion or allotment there.
rows.anchor: أي: من نصيب ولا حظ

words: وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemnation is intended to deter people from resembling those who ask only for worldly benefit.
rows.anchor: وتضمن هذا الذم التنفير عن التشبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says some Bedouins at the pilgrimage standing place asked for a rainy, fertile year and good offspring but mentioned nothing about the Hereafter; the verse censures them.
rows.anchor: كان قوم من الأعراب يجيئون إلى الموقف، فيقولون

words: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةًۭ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says believers who came after the Bedouins asked for good in both worlds and protection from the Fire, and the following verse was revealed concerning them.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

words: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةًۭ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises those who ask for good in this world and the next; this prayer gathers every good and wards off every evil.
rows.anchor: فجمعت هذه الدعوة كل خير في الدنيا، وصرفت كل شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly good encompasses desirable benefits including health, a spacious home, a good spouse, ample provision, useful knowledge, righteous deeds, comfortable transport, and fine reputation; commentators’ lists are compatible.
rows.anchor: من عافية، ودار رحبة، وزوجة حسنة، ورزق واسع، وعلم نافع، وعمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest good in the Hereafter is entry into Paradise, along with safety from the great terror at the gathering and an easy reckoning.
rows.anchor: أعلى ذلك دخول الجنة وتوابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation from the Fire entails making its causes easier to avoid in worldly life by shunning prohibitions, sins, doubtful matters, and unlawful things.
rows.anchor: من اجتناب المحارم والآثام وترك الشبهات والحرام

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In a report from ʿUmar, he repeatedly asks God for a clear ruling on wine: first this verse is revealed, then 4:43 bars approaching prayer while drunk, and finally 5:90–91 commands abstention, to which ʿUmar replies that they desist.
rows.anchor: عن عمر أنه قال: لما نزل تحريم الخمر قال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is transmitted by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i through Israel from Abu Ishaq, and by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh through al-Thawri; Abu Zurʿa says Abu Maysara did not hear from ʿUmar, while Ibn al-Madini calls the chain sound and al-Tirmidhi authenticates it.
rows.anchor: أبو زرعة: لم يسمع منه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim adds ʿUmar’s explanation that wine makes wealth and reason disappear.
rows.anchor: وزاد ابن أبي حاتم -بعد قوله: انتهينا -: إنها تذهب المال وتذهب العقل

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar defines wine as anything that clouds the intellect; Ibn Kathir says the definition will be explained further in the commentary on al-Ma’ida.
rows.anchor: إنه كل ما خامر العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means gambling.
rows.anchor: وكذا الميسر، وهو القمار

words: قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌۭ كَبِيرٌۭ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine’s sins concern religion, while its benefits are worldly: bodily benefit, digestion, elimination, sharpening some minds, and the pleasure of intoxication; gambling winnings could also support a person or family.
rows.anchor: أما إثمهما فهو في الدين، وأما المنافع فدنيوية

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit’s pre-Islamic verse depicts drinkers as becoming kings and lions undeterred by battle, illustrating wine’s intoxicating pleasure.
rows.anchor: ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا … وأسدا لا ينهنهها اللقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other worldly gains included selling wine and spending its price, or using gambling proceeds for oneself or one’s family.
rows.anchor: وكذا بيعها والانتفاع بثمنها. وما كان يقمشه بعضهم من الميسر فينفقه على نفسه أو عياله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those benefits do not outweigh the greater harm to intellect and religion; the verse prepares for wine’s categorical prohibition by implication, before 5:90–91 states it explicitly.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كانت هذه الآية ممهدة لتحريم الخمر على البتات، ولم تكن مصرحة بل معرضة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر، والشعبي، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: These authorities say this was the first verse revealed about wine; the verse in al-Nisa’ followed, then the verses in al-Ma’ida, which made wine unlawful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر، والشعبي، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
